scope_note: Follow-on to heuristic-stochastic-miners.json (W4PM-LEAN-GALL-018). That checkpoint established genetic mining, ACO, and PSO (wasm4pm/src/genetic_discovery.rs) are no_lean_coverage and stochastic by construction. This checkpoint asks a narrower question: separate from the intractable actual-optimization-quality claim, is there any genuinely deterministic, RNG-independent, formally provable structural property connecting these three algorithms to a Lean-style theorem -- specifically the elitism/monotonic-improvement pattern (best-fitness-never-decreases-across-iterations). Answer: yes for GA and PSO, as-shipped-output NO for ACO (a specific, code-cited hole, not a generic 'stochastic' hand-wave).

ledger_entries.theorem_sketch: For fixed (log, activity_key, population_size >= 2) and any generation counts g <= g', if discover_genetic_algorithm_from_log(log, key, population_size, g) = Some(_, f) and discover_genetic_algorithm_from_log(log, key, population_size, g') = Some(_, f'), then f' >= f. Informal Lean-style: theorem ga_best_fitness_monotone (pop : Nat) (hpop : pop >= 2) (g g' : Nat) (hg : g <= g') : bestFitness log key pop g <= bestFitness log key pop g' := by induction on (g' - g), each extra generation step preserving the invariant via the elite-copy lemma below.
ledger_entries.why_rng_independent: wasm4pm/src/genetic_discovery.rs, discover_genetic_algorithm_from_log (lines ~140-166): each generation, `population.sort_unstable_by(|a,b| b.1.total_cmp(&a.1))` sorts descending by fitness, then `let mut next = population[..elite_size].to_vec();` copies the top elite_size = (population_size/4).max(1) tuples VERBATIM (both EdgeSet and its already-computed f64 fitness) into `next` before any mutation/crossover is applied to the remaining slots. The elite slice is never touched by `crossover_edges_seeded`/`mutate_edges_seeded` afterward -- only the newly-generated children filling `next` up to population_size are. Consequence: population[0].1 (the max fitness) at generation g+1 is provably >= population[0].1 at generation g, because the generation-g best individual (whichever RNG draws produced it) is a literal element of generation g+1's population, unchanged. This holds for EVERY possible RNG trace -- the argument never inspects what the RNG drew, only that `next[..elite_size]` is a syntactic copy of `population[..elite_size]` pre-sort-descending. Ties in fitness (total_cmp on f64, non-stable sort) do not threaten the claim: the property is about the VALUE of the maximum, not the identity of which tied individual is retained.
ledger_entries.hole_check: Checked and ruled out as holes: (1) fitness recompute divergence -- elite fitness values are carried as already-computed f64s, never recomputed post-copy, so no floating-point non-monotonicity from re-evaluation; (2) mutation of the elite itself -- confirmed absent, `next[..elite_size]` bypasses `mutate_edges_seeded` entirely, only post-elite-slice children go through crossover+mutation; (3) elite_size=0 edge case -- `(population_size/4).max(1)` guarantees elite_size >= 1 whenever population_size >= 2 is satisfied by the existing parameter-validation guard (population_size < 2 => None), so at least the single best individual always survives. No hole found for this property as currently coded.

rust_side.test: wasm4pm/tests/algorithm_correctness.rs:110 ga_convergence_more_generations_never_worse -- asserts f100 >= f1 - 1e-9, exactly this property (up to float tolerance) at 20 population_size, 1 vs 100 generations.

ledger_entries.theorem_sketch: For fixed (log, activity_key, swarm_size >= 1) and any iteration counts i <= i', if discover_pso_algorithm_from_log(log, key, swarm_size, i) = Some(_, f) and discover_pso_algorithm_from_log(log, key, swarm_size, i') = Some(_, f'), then f' >= f. Informal Lean-style: theorem pso_global_best_monotone (swarm : Nat) (hswarm : swarm >= 1) (i i' : Nat) (hi : i <= i') : bestGlobalFitness log key swarm i <= bestGlobalFitness log key swarm i' := by induction on (i' - i), each extra iteration step preserving best_global via the strict-improvement-only-assignment lemma below.
ledger_entries.why_rng_independent: wasm4pm/src/genetic_discovery.rs, discover_pso_algorithm_from_log: `best_global: Option<(EdgeSet, f64)>` is initialized during particle spawn (`if best_global.is_none() || fitness > best_global.as_ref().unwrap().1 { best_global = Some(...) }`) and updated identically inside the per-iteration per-particle loop (`if new_fitness > best_global.as_ref().unwrap().1 { best_global = Some((edge_set.clone(), new_fitness)); }`). This is the cleanest possible RNG-independent monotone-max pattern: `best_global.1` is assigned a new value ONLY when that value is strictly greater than the current one -- by definition of this control-flow shape, the sequence of best_global.1 values over the run's timeline is non-decreasing, for any sequence of RNG draws whatsoever (the RNG determines WHICH edge sets are tried and WHAT their fitness values are, never whether a worse value overwrites best_global). This is strictly simpler than GA's elite-copy argument -- no auxiliary lemma about population slicing is needed, just the direct semantics of `if x > best { best = x }`.
ledger_entries.hole_check: Checked and ruled out: (1) best_global read via `.as_ref().unwrap()` inside the loop condition and the update on the same line -- no intervening mutation of best_global between the comparison and the assignment (single-threaded, sequential); (2) NaN/Inf fitness -- unlike ACO, discover_pso_algorithm_from_log has no explicit `is_finite()` sanitization on `new_fitness` before the `>` comparison; if `evaluate_edges_fitness` ever returned NaN, `NaN > x` is false in IEEE 754 so best_global would simply never update from a NaN candidate (a NaN can never win the comparison) -- this does not break monotonicity of best_global.1 itself (a NaN is never stored), though it does mean a NaN-valued particle silently never contributes, an orthogonal (and currently unobserved) concern noted here but not rated as breaking this specific claim. (3) no fallback-substitution step of the kind ACO has post-loop -- the function returns `best_global?` directly (edges, fitness) unmodified after the iteration loop, so the returned value IS `best_global.1`, with no post-processing step that could break the streak. This is why PSO does NOT have ACO's hole (see below).

rust_side.test: wasm4pm/tests/algorithm_correctness.rs:183 pso_convergence_more_iterations_never_worse -- asserts f50 >= f5 - 1e-9, exactly this property (up to float tolerance) at 20 swarm_size, 5 vs 50 iterations.

ledger_entries.theorem_sketch: RULED OUT as stated for the function's RETURNED value. The internal per-iteration tracked quantity `best_solution.1` (before the post-loop fallback substitution) DOES follow the identical strict-> assignment pattern as PSO's best_global and IS itself RNG-independently monotone in iteration/ant count by the same argument. However, `discover_aco_algorithm_from_log`'s final `.map(...)` closure performs a conditional substitution: `if edges.is_empty() { use a freshly-computed fallback_fitness over the full edge vocabulary } else { use (edges, fitness) as tracked }`. `fallback_fitness` is NOT compared against, and has no proven relationship to, `best_solution.1` from any other run at any other iteration count -- it is an independently computed fitness value over a completely different edge set (the full observed DFG, not any set the ants explored). Consequence: a NO-general-theorem-of-this-shape holds for the RETURNED fitness as a function of iteration count, because a run at low iteration count that lands in the empty-edge-set branch returns fallback_fitness (a value with no ordering guarantee relative to a higher-iteration-count run's best_solution.1), and a run at higher iteration count could plausibly avoid the empty-edge-set branch (nonempty best_solution) or vice versa, with no code-level guarantee about which branch is more likely as iterations grow. This is a genuine, code-identified hole -- not a restatement of 'ACO is stochastic'.
ledger_entries.why_rng_independent: N/A as stated (ruled out) -- the internal-only sub-claim about best_solution.1 alone (ignoring the fallback branch) IS RNG-independent by the identical reasoning as PSO's best_global (see pso entry): `if best_solution.is_none() || fitness > best_solution.as_ref().unwrap().1 { best_solution = Some((ant_edges.clone(), fitness)); }` inside the ant loop, run every iteration, is the same strict-greater-only-assignment shape. This narrower, unobservable (never returned directly) internal invariant is not ruled out -- only the claim about the function's actual output is.
ledger_entries.hole_check: The hole, precisely: wasm4pm/src/genetic_discovery.rs, discover_aco_algorithm_from_log's final `best_solution.map(|(edges, fitness)| { let (final_edges, final_fitness) = if edges.is_empty() { let fallback_fitness = evaluate_edges_fitness(&edge_vocab.iter().copied().collect(), &col, vocab_len); (edge_vocab..., fallback_fitness.is_finite()-guarded) } else { (edges, fitness) }; ... })`. No max(fallback_fitness, best_solution.1) or equivalent guard exists -- the branch fully replaces the tracked best with an uncompared value whenever edges.is_empty(). This is the W4PM-LEAN-GALL-018 degenerate-result fix itself (an intentional, already-shipped correctness fix, not a new bug) -- but it is also, as an unavoidable side effect, the reason ACO's output-level monotonicity claim cannot be proven as-is. No `aco_convergence_more_iterations_never_worse` test exists in algorithm_correctness.rs (confirmed absent by direct read of the test file, unlike the GA and PSO analogs at lines 110 and 183) -- consistent with this hole; such a test would not reliably pass across parameter sweeps that straddle the empty/nonempty boundary.

rust_side.test: wasm4pm/tests/algorithm_correctness.rs:628 aco_never_returns_empty_dfg_on_nontrivial_input -- tests the fallback's PRESENCE (non-empty output), not monotonicity; no convergence-never-worse test exists for ACO, confirmed by direct inspection.

optimization_quality_claim.scope: GA / ACO / PSO all: the claim that the returned solution is 'good' or 'near-optimal' relative to a well-defined optimum over the DFG edge-subset search space -- as distinct from the elitism_monotonicity claims above, which are about the algorithm's own best-tracked-value trajectory, not about that value's distance to any true optimum.
reasons: Unbounded/combinatorial solution space: the search space is the powerset of edge_vocab (2^|edge_vocab| candidate DFGs), which grows exponentially in the number of distinct directly-follows pairs observed in the log -- no bound on |edge_vocab| is established anywhere in genetic_discovery.rs; it is exactly the number of distinct (from,to) pairs seen, unconstrained by any code-level cap.

No convexity/submodularity structure established: evaluate_edges_fitness (utilities.rs, called identically by all three algorithms) is a black-box coverage function over traces; the code makes no claim, comment, or proof-adjacent structure (no monotone-submodular argument, no convex relaxation, no matroid structure) that would make a greedy or local-search procedure provably near-optimal (e.g. no (1-1/e) submodular-maximization-style guarantee is claimed or derivable from the code as written). Region theory or matroid arguments that WOULD license such a guarantee for DFG discovery specifically do not appear in mfact or mfw (see ledger_entries in heuristic-stochastic-miners.json for ilp-petri-net, the one algorithm where such theory is at least in-principle relevant and still absent).

RNG source not analyzed for the statistical-independence properties a probabilistic Lean proof would require: all three algorithms construct `StdRng::seed_from_u64(42)` locally (flagged as an architectural inconsistency in W4PM-LEAN-GALL-018, not fixed there or here) rather than using the project's documented support::rng::seeded_rng() convention. Even setting that inconsistency aside, StdRng (rand crate's ChaCha12-based generator) has no accompanying analysis in this codebase of the statistical independence or distributional properties (e.g. genuine uniformity of gen::<f64>() draws over successive calls, absence of correlation across the many sequential draws consumed per ant/particle/individual) that any convergence-in-probability theorem (the only kind of optimization-quality claim that could even in principle be stated for a stochastic search) would need as a hypothesis. No such analysis exists in mfact, mfw, or this codebase.

Consequence: even a convergence-in-probability claim (the weakest form of optimization-quality claim that survives the stochasticity) is not merely unproven but not yet well-defined in this codebase -- it would require first (a) a bound or asymptotic characterization of |edge_vocab| growth, (b) an established structural property (submodularity or similar) of evaluate_edges_fitness over the edge-subset lattice, and (c) a formalized independence model for the RNG draws, none of which exist. This is a stronger and more specific claim than the general 'these are stochastic algorithms' observation from W4PM-LEAN-GALL-018 -- it names the exact three missing prerequisites.

mfact_mfw_search.method: mcp__plugin_lumen_lumen__semantic_search against /Users/sac/mfact and /Users/sac/mfw for 'monotone non-decreasing sequence lemma elitism hill climbing invariant best-so-far'
mfact_mfw_search.result: No genuine Lean-formalized monotone-sequence, elitism, or hill-climbing-invariant lemma found in either repo that could serve as a carrier for the GA/PSO claims above. Top mfact hits were process-mining-adjacent (Little's Law, attention-conservation interval combinatorics, Gibbs' inequality) and Lean-audit/tactic-search meta-material, none touching population-based or greedy-best-tracking invariants. Top mfw hits were an escort-distribution Rust unit test (higher_q_concentrates_mass_on_the_largest_input, tools/mfw-cli/src/verbs/cmca.rs) and various LSP/thesis prose docs -- the escort-distribution test is a monotonicity-flavored assertion in Rust, not a Lean theorem, and is about a different mathematical object (Renyi/escort-distribution mass concentration under q) with no genuine carrier map to elitism-based population search. Per this program's LEAN_NAME_MATCH_WITHOUT_CARRIER_MAP refusal rule, this superficial thematic proximity is explicitly NOT treated as coverage -- no match is claimed.
mfact_mfw_search.not_claimed: Any existing Lean asset in mfact or mfw covers, informs, or could be directly reused for the GA/PSO elitism-monotonicity theorem sketches above. Both sketches would require new Lean work from scratch if ever pursued.

comparison_mode_note: N/A this checkpoint -- no Lean-side formula exists for any of the 3 algorithms' elitism-monotonicity or optimization-quality claims. GA and PSO's theorem sketches are proposed FUTURE targets (informal statements about existing Rust control flow), not claims of an existing Rust<->Lean correspondence.
achieved_evidence_class_summary: GA: tractable_future_target (elitism-copy pattern, RNG-independent, no code-level hole found). PSO: tractable_future_target (direct strict-> best-tracking, RNG-independent, cleanest of the three, no code-level hole found). ACO: ruled_out_for_shipped_output (the fallback-to-raw-DFG substitution on empty edge sets breaks monotonicity of the RETURNED fitness across iteration counts; the internal best_solution.1 before that substitution would itself satisfy the same clean argument as PSO, but is never returned directly). Optimization-quality claim for all 3: UNSUPPORTED, with three specific named missing prerequisites (unbounded search space, no submodularity/convexity structure, no RNG-independence analysis) rather than a generic stochasticity dismissal.
not_claimed: That any Lean proof of the GA or PSO elitism-monotonicity theorem sketches exists (none does -- these are proposed future targets only); that ACO's internal best_solution monotonicity claim has been formally stated or proven (noted as plausible by analogy to PSO, not itself verified with a test or proof); that the optimization-quality claim is merely 'hard' rather than currently ill-posed in this codebase (the three missing prerequisites are named specifically, not asserted as a vague difficulty); that mfact/mfw contain any reusable Lean material for this program (explicitly searched and not found, per the refusal-rule discipline).
